documents.title: can I get in
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hey, I've dropped a bunch of weight without trying, like 15 lbs since summer, and my nose keeps bleeding on and off. Also not sleeping great. My buddies keep telling me I'm cranky lately lol. Can I come in next week? Mornings are best.

documents.title: RE: can I get in
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Good morning Malcolm, you're set for Monday 2/10 at 8:15 with the doctor. If the nosebleeds get heavy or won't stop with pressure, call us right away.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 29M, last seen at his physical in August. About six months of unintended weight loss, ~15 lb by his count, says he's eating and exercising the same as always. On-and-off nosebleeds, usually small, stop with pressure. Trouble falling and staying asleep. Friends have told him he's been short-tempered and moody. No fevers, night sweats, cough, GI symptoms. Still smoking a pack a day; alcohol unchanged by his account. Asked directly about drugs, he deflected.

O: HR 110. Wt 74.2 kg (81 in Aug). Restless, shifting in the chair, otherwise appears well. Nasal mucosa red and inflamed with a perforation of the septum. No cervical, supraclavicular or axillary nodes. Heart tachycardic, regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin unremarkable. Neuro nonfocal.
PHQ-9 7.

Labs drawn in office, back this afternoon: Hgb 14.2, WBC 7.0, plt 250, random glucose 98, Cr 1.0.

A/P
Weight loss with recurrent epistaxis, a perforated septum, insomnia, irritability and a resting tachycardia in a young man. Counts and chemistry unremarkable. The nasal exam in particular raises concern for intranasal stimulant use. Urine drug screen sent, explained why and he agreed to give the sample.
- Will call with tox result and bring him back to talk it through
- Smoking: advised to quit, not today

documents.title: Result call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Per PCP, called pt re: urine screen. Reached him on cell, verified DOB. Told him the screen was positive for cocaine and negative for everything else on the panel, and that the doctor would like to see him in person to go over it. He was quiet, then said ok. Booked Wed 2/19 at 4:30.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back to discuss the positive screen. More open today. Has been snorting cocaine, mostly on weekends, sometimes at work events, for about a year. Says it started socially and he figured he had it under control. Connects the nosebleeds and weight to it once we talk it through.

Exam: more settled than last week. Septum perforated as before, no active bleeding.

A/P
Cocaine abuse, intranasal.
- Went over the septal damage, the risk to his heart (spikes in pressure and rate, arrhythmia, MI even at his age), and the family history of addiction on his dad's side and early heart disease in his grandfather.
- Offered referral to an outpatient addiction treatment program. He would rather try to cut back on his own for now. Order withdrawn at his request, offer left open.
- Combined with cigarettes, his cardiac risk is real. Quitline again.
- Recheck weight and how he's doing in 2 months.

documents.title: We missed you
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Malcolm, we had you on the schedule yesterday morning for your follow-up. Please reply or call to rebook, the doctor would like to see you.

documents.title: RE: We missed you
documents.author: patient
documents.body: sorry, been slammed. can do early June

documents.title: RE: We missed you
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: You're booked Monday 6/9 at 7:45.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Says he has cut way back, still uses "once in a while." No nosebleeds in the past month. Sleep a little better. Weight about flat, 74.5. Smoking the same.
Nose: perforation unchanged, mucosa less angry. Heart regular, lungs clear.
A/P: Cocaine abuse, reports reduced use. Raised the treatment program again, he declined; he knows how to reach me if that changes. Tobacco cessation advised. Follow up in fall.

events.reason: Palpitations, anxiety and chest discomfort after cocaine

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia, rate 124. Normal axis. PR, QRS and QT intervals within normal limits. No ST-segment elevation or depression. No T-wave inversions.

documents.title: Emergency Department Provider Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 10/13/2025 23:40. Departure 10/14/2025 04:50.
Allergies: NKDA. Home medications: none.

CC: heart racing, chest discomfort

HPI: 30 y/o M walked in with a friend. Was at a party and roughly half an hour before arrival snorted a white powder, which he then told us was cocaine. Abrupt onset of pounding heartbeat and anxiety, mild chest discomfort, nonradiating. Describes himself as wired and on edge. Friend says he was fine earlier in the evening. Denies fever, chills, cough, recent illness. Known prior cocaine use per pt; smokes ~1 ppd; drinks socially. FHx notable for early CAD in a grandfather.

Exam: T 37.1 C, HR 126, RR 20, BP 164/92, SpO2 98% RA. Anxious, fidgety, alert and oriented. Heart: regular, fast, no murmurs, rubs or gallops. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abd soft. Neuro: alert, fluent, moves all extremities, no focal deficit.

ECG (23:48): sinus tachycardia, no ST changes.

ED course: lorazepam 2 mg IV and aspirin 325 mg PO chewed. hs-troponin I 3 ng/L at 23:55 and 4 ng/L at 02:55. CBC and BMP within normal limits. Urine cocaine screen positive. Heart rate and anxiety settled over the next hours. At 04:30 HR 94, BP 134/82, chest discomfort resolved.

Impression: acute cocaine intoxication with sympathomimetic symptoms; MI ruled out by serial troponins and ECG.

Disposition: discharged home with friend. Counseled to avoid cocaine; return precautions for chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath. Follow up with PCP within 1 week. Copy to PCP.

documents.title: ED record received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: ED provider note, ECG tracing and labs from the regional hospital for 10/13 overnight visit received electronically. Routed to PCP inbox.

documents.title: ED record review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed. Cocaine intoxication, troponins negative x2, ECG sinus tach only. Asked front desk to reach him for a visit this week or next.

documents.title: after the ER
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I guess you saw I ended up in the ER Monday night. That scared me. I'm ready to talk about the program you mentioned. When can I come in

documents.title: RE: after the ER
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you reached out, and glad you're ok. I have Monday 10/20 at 8:00 if that works; the front desk will confirm. If you get chest pain or your heart races again, go straight back to the ER.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen one week after ED visit for cocaine intoxication (palpitations, chest discomfort; serial troponins and ECG reassuring per their record). Feels back to baseline. No chest pain, palpitations or SOB since.

Much more forthcoming today. Use never really came down after our June visit; mostly weekends but some weeknights, cravings when he's out with clients, spends more than he means to, has tried to stop several times and couldn't, kept using knowing about his nose, and now the ER. No cocaine since that night, he says. Drinking a little less. Still 1 ppd.

Exam: HR and BP normal today. Wt 75.0. Calm, good eye contact. Septal perforation unchanged, no bleeding. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear.
PHQ-9 5. AUDIT-C 4.

A/P
1. Cocaine use disorder, severe (updated from cocaine abuse; meets criteria on today's history). He's ready. Referral to outpatient addiction treatment program placed, he'll call for intake this week. Release signed so they can send notes. No medication indicated.
2. Acute cocaine intoxication: resolved.
3. Tobacco use disorder: advised to quit; he wants to tackle one thing at a time.
4. Flu and COVID given.
Telehealth check-in in a few months.

documents.title: Outpatient Addiction Program Intake
documents.author: addiction medicine
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT SUBSTANCE USE TREATMENT PROGRAM — INTAKE SUMMARY
Date of intake: 11/06/2025
Referred by: primary care physician
Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none.

Mr. Kirby is a 30-year-old sales representative referred after an ED visit for cocaine intoxication on 10/13/2025. He describes intranasal cocaine use beginning about early 2024, escalating over 2024-2025, with cravings, repeated unsuccessful attempts to stop, money and time spent, sleep and mood effects, use in risky settings, and continued use despite nasal septal damage and the ED visit. He reports no cocaine since 10/13/2025. Smokes about 1 pack per day. Drinks socially. Father with alcohol use disorder.

Diagnoses: Cocaine use disorder, severe, in early abstinence. Tobacco use disorder.

Plan: weekly group cognitive behavioral therapy plus individual counseling; random urine drug screens; tobacco cessation resources offered. No pharmacotherapy indicated. We will update the referring office periodically with patient consent.

Intake clinician, outpatient addiction program

documents.title: Letter review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Intake letter read. Good that he followed through. Nothing to change.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from his car on lunch break, consented to telehealth, identity verified.
Going to group every week and seeing his counselor. No cocaine since October, he says, and the urine screens there have been clean. Sleeping much better. No nosebleeds. Thinks he's put a few pounds back on. Still about a pack a day; the cigarettes are what he leans on now.
Appears well on video, speech normal, upbeat.
A/P: Cocaine use disorder, severe, in early remission by report, engaged in treatment. Keep going. Tobacco: offered nicotine patches with a short-acting form for cravings, declined for now, maybe in the summer. Physical in August.

documents.title: Treatment Progress Update
documents.author: addiction medicine
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT SUBSTANCE USE TREATMENT PROGRAM — PROGRESS UPDATE
Report date: 03/12/2026

Patient has attended group and individual sessions consistently since intake in November. All random urine drug screens have been negative. He continues to report abstinence from cocaine. Tobacco use ongoing; cessation resources re-offered.

Given his engagement, sessions are stepped down to every other week. Diagnoses unchanged: cocaine use disorder, severe; tobacco use disorder. No medications.

Counselor, outpatient addiction program

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
31M, yearly. Doing well. Still in the program every other week, no cocaine since last October by his report. Work going fine. Weight back up to 78. Sleeping normally. Drinks less than he used to. Still 1 ppd.

Meds: none. NKDA. FHx unchanged.
ROS: no chest pain, palpitations, nosebleeds, cough or SOB.

Exam: well-appearing, relaxed. Wt 78.0. Septal perforation unchanged in size, mucosa healed, no crusting or bleeding. Oropharynx clear. No adenopathy. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema. Skin normal. Mood euthymic.
PHQ-9 3. AUDIT-C 4.

A/P
1. Cocaine use disorder, severe, sustained abstinence by report since 10/2025, engaged in treatment. Proud of him and told him so.
2. Tobacco use disorder: brief counseling; he'd like to try quitting after a big work conference this fall, we'll revisit then.
3. Preventive: CBC, CMP, lipids today. Flu/COVID in the fall.

RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Your physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Malcolm, everything from Friday came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver panel, cholesterol. Good visit. Let me know when you're ready to try the patches.

documents.title: RE: Your physical labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Awesome, thanks. Will do.
